elements.element: Renewal must use one of the two permitted models: renewal only by mutual written agreement, or automatic renewal subject to the preferred safeguards.
elements.evidence: Section 8.2 uses the permitted automatic-renewal model; therefore, the automatic-renewal safeguards apply.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term must be 12 months.
elements.evidence: Section 8.2 states that each Order Form “renews for twelve months.”

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out by giving 30 days' advance written notice.
elements.evidence: Section 8.2 permits “either Party,” which includes Customer, to prevent renewal by giving 30 days' advance written notice.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must give Customer a written renewal reminder at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: The added operative sentence requires Vendor to give Customer written notice of each upcoming renewal at least 60 days before renewal.

elements.element: Renewal price increases must be capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%.
elements.evidence: Section 8.3 caps increases to recurring Fees on renewal at the lesser of the preceding 12-month increase in CPI-U and 3%.
Section 8.2 provides that each Order Form renews unless timely notice is given.

elements.element: The required non-renewal notice window must be no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Section 8.2 requires 30 days' advance written notice, which is less than the 60-day maximum.

elements.element: Renewal price increases must not exceed 5%.
elements.evidence: Section 8.3 caps renewal increases at the lesser of CPI-U and 3%, which is necessarily no more than 5%.

result.reason: The redline satisfies the preferred automatic-renewal alternative: 12-month renewals, a 30-day Customer opt-out right, a Vendor reminder at least 60 days before renewal, and the CPI/3% cap. It also satisfies every fallback requirement. The changes are limited to shortening the notice period and adding the required reminder, without disturbing unrelated term provisions or introducing a contradiction.
